quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #19
										  					
  

35 Questions • Passing Score 30

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: You must drive at the posted speed.
The maximum legal speed on this road is 55 mph.
You must drive through the intersection at the posted speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum legal speed on this road is 55 mph.
questions.explanation: This is a speed limit sign. It shows the fastest speed you can legally drive on this road. In bad weather like rain, snow, or ice, you should drive slower than the posted limit.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Construction workers on or near the road.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. They warn drivers about hazards ahead. This sign means people may be crossing the road ahead.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Traffic only moves in the direction the arrow points.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic only moves in the direction the arrow points.
questions.explanation: This one-way sign shows that traffic can only move in the direction the arrow is pointing.

questions.question: Where are you not allowed to park?

options.text: Within 15 feet of a fire hydrant.
Within 50 feet of a railroad crossing.

questions.explanation: You cannot park within 15 feet of a fire hydrant, within 20 feet of an intersection, or within 50 feet of a railroad crossing.

questions.question: If you are in another driver's blind spot, what should you do?

options.text: Move forward or backward so the other driver can see you.
Honk your horn to warn them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move forward or backward so the other driver can see you.
questions.explanation: Never stay in another driver's blind spot. Move forward or backward so the other driver can see you.

questions.question: Only vehicles with special disability plates or placards may park in spaces marked for people with disabilities.
questions.explanation: Parking spaces marked for people with disabilities can only be used by vehicles with disability license plates, Disabled Veteran plates, or disability parking placards.

questions.question: What shape and color is a slow-moving vehicle sign?
questions.explanation: The slow-moving vehicle sign is a reflective orange triangle. Vehicles with this sign are traveling 25 mph or slower.

questions.question: Which statement is true about passing?

options.text: Signal at least 100 feet before passing and check for oncoming traffic.
Use mirrors and look over your left shoulder to check your blind spot.
Wait until you see both headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror before returning to your lane.

questions.explanation: Always signal at least 100 feet before passing. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder. Wait until you can see both headlights of the other car in your rearview mirror before moving back to your lane.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Slow down when the pavement is wet.
The road ahead has a series of turns or curves.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down when the pavement is wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road is slippery when wet. In wet conditions, slow down, avoid sudden braking or steering, and keep more distance from the car ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. They warn drivers about hazards ahead. This sign means the road may be slippery when wet, making vehicles harder to control.

questions.question: What does a red arrow on a traffic light mean?

options.text: Stop, then go when the way is clear.
Stop, then go when the light turns green or a green arrow appears.
You can turn in the direction the red arrow points.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, then go when the light turns green or a green arrow appears.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means you must stop completely. Wait until the light turns green or a green arrow appears before you go.

questions.question: What does a "No stopping" sign mean?

options.text: You can stop to unload packages.
You can stop only to avoid hitting another vehicle.
You can stop to let passengers out.
You can stop for less than five minutes.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can stop only to avoid hitting another vehicle.
questions.explanation: A "No stopping" sign means you can only stop to obey a traffic signal, obey a police officer, or prevent a crash with another vehicle.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Drive carefully and be ready to stop.

questions.explanation: An eight-sided sign always means "stop." You must come to a complete stop and wait for vehicles and pedestrians to pass before going.

questions.question: If you get stranded in a snowstorm, what should you do?

options.text: Leave your car and walk to get help.
Lie down in your car and sleep.
Walk into the road to get other drivers' attention.
Stay in your car. People will find you more easily if you stay with your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your car. People will find you more easily if you stay with your vehicle.
questions.explanation: If you get stranded in a snowstorm, stay in your car and wait for help. You are more likely to be found if you stay with your vehicle. Walking in a snowstorm is dangerous.

questions.question: If a bus is signaling to enter the road after a stop, what must you do?

options.text: Honk to tell them you are there.
Speed up to pass the bus.

questions.explanation: You must yield to any bus that is signaling to enter the road after stopping. Slow down, change lanes, or stop to let the bus safely enter traffic.

questions.question: At a light rail intersection, you should always:

options.text: Look both ways before crossing the tracks.
Pay attention and follow all traffic signals.
Share the road with pedestrians and bicyclists.

questions.explanation: Never drive around lowered crossing gates. Always look both ways before crossing tracks and obey all signs and traffic signals. Trains share the road with cars and bicyclists.

questions.question: When driving near large trucks, what must other drivers account for?

options.text: Large trucks need more distance to stop.
Large trucks need less distance to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks need more distance to stop.
questions.explanation: When driving near large trucks, other drivers must account for the extra stopping distance trucks need. Stay in places where the truck driver can see you and where large vehicles don't block your view.

questions.question: When is it important to slow down?

options.text: When the road is wet or slippery.

questions.explanation: Slow down on narrow or winding roads, near intersections, near railroad crossings, on hills, on curves, near pedestrians, and when roads are wet or slippery.

questions.question: When should you drive below the posted speed limit?

options.text: When driving conditions are not perfect.
When you see a police car.
When entering a highway with other cars.
When you are on a four-lane road.

questions.correctAnswerText: When driving conditions are not perfect.
questions.explanation: Drive below the speed limit when roads are wet, when visibility is poor, or when anything else makes conditions unsafe. You can be ticketed for speeding even if you are within the posted limit.

questions.question: If an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is near you, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up to get out of the way.
Stop immediately and block the vehicle.
Do everything you can to clear a path for the emergency vehicle.
Signal to the emergency vehicle when it is safe to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do everything you can to clear a path for the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is near you, do everything you can to clear a path. If it is safe, pull to the side of the road to let the emergency vehicle pass.

questions.question: You must use your headlights when you use your windshield wipers because of bad weather.
questions.explanation: You must use your headlights when you use your windshield wipers because of bad weather.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a roundabout is ahead. Enter slowly and give the right of way to cars already in the roundabout.

questions.question: What can you do from the center lane?
questions.explanation: The center lane is only for left turns from either direction. You cannot use it for passing or driving straight through.

questions.question: When driving on an interstate, what should you do?

options.text: Stop on the shoulder if you are tired.
Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Always signal, check your mirrors, and check your blind spots before changing lanes or passing. Only stop on the shoulder during an emergency. Change lanes rarely. Do not use cruise control in heavy traffic or bad weather.

questions.question: How does alcohol affect your reflexes and judgment?

options.text: Beer has less effect than wine.
Wine has less effect than beer.
Hard ciders and mixed drinks have the most effect.
It depends on how much alcohol is in your blood.

questions.correctAnswerText: It depends on how much alcohol is in your blood.
questions.explanation: Any type of alcohol can harm your reflexes and judgment. The type of alcohol does not matter. Only the amount of alcohol in your bloodstream matters.

questions.question: You are driving up a hill and see a heavy truck ahead. What should you know?

options.text: The truck may be going slower than the speed limit.
You may not be able to safely pass the truck.
You may not be able to legally pass the truck.

questions.explanation: Large trucks often go slower than the speed limit, especially on hills. Be careful when approaching them from behind. On hills with poor visibility, passing is not allowed.

questions.question: What can reduce road rage and aggressive driving?
questions.explanation: To prevent road rage, use turn signals, obey speed limits, and leave plenty of time for your trip.

questions.question: When passing on a multilane highway, what should you do?

options.text: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
There is no need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Before passing, make sure the passing lane is clear and use your turn signal to show you are changing lanes.

questions.question: At what blood alcohol content (BAC) are you legally considered to be driving under the influence?
questions.explanation: Drivers age 21 and older with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher are driving under the influence. If your driving is impaired, you can be convicted even with a lower BAC. Drivers under 21 can be convicted with a BAC of 0.02 percent or higher.

questions.question: What should you do if you see an animal on the road?

options.text: Pass the animal as close as possible.

questions.explanation: Always be very careful when you see an animal on the road. Pass it slowly to avoid scaring it.

questions.question: What does this black and yellow sign mean?

options.text: The road to the right is one-way only.
There is a detour to the right due to roadwork.
Slow down. The road ahead makes a sharp turn.
There is a crossroad to your right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down. The road ahead makes a sharp turn.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road ahead curves sharply. You should slow down before reaching the curve, just like you would at an intersection turn.

questions.question: When can you drive across a dashed white line?

options.text: When it is safe to change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it is safe to change lanes.
questions.explanation: Dashed white lines separate lanes going the same direction. You can cross them to change lanes or pass if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching an accident scene?

options.text: Keep your attention on your driving.
Stop only if you are involved or emergency help has not arrived.

questions.explanation: Do not stop at an accident unless you are involved or emergency help has not arrived. Stay focused on driving and keep moving. Watch for people on or near the road. Do not drive to an accident, fire, or disaster just to look.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, you must yield to drivers who arrived before you.
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, yield the right-of-way to drivers who arrived first. Wait your turn to enter the intersection.

questions.question: What should a driver do before taking a non-prescription drug?

options.text: Read the labels for warnings about driving.
Continue driving no matter what the labels say.

questions.correctAnswerText: Read the labels for warnings about driving.
questions.explanation: Many over-the-counter drugs can affect your driving. Check medication labels for warnings, even for cold or allergy remedies. Ask your doctor or pharmacist if a drug is safe to take before driving.
